followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Moldova COVID crossing restrictions as a formal policy observation, rather than a reconstructed complete operational spell. Preserve the named closed/active post distinction and Ocnița road-versus-rail and Criva rail-versus-road differences. Partial and general later notices retain their own exemptions and traveller restrictions. Retain the 17 March 2020 00:00 legal onset and unknown common endpoint, with no numerical duration. The two-post November notice and prospective 24 May 2021 restoration do not prove one common actual reopening or uninterrupted prior closure. Retain Health and biosecurity / Human disease control as the stated pandemic rationale. All three inspected sources are official border-police notices; publication dates not exposed by the rendering remain unknown. They are policy documents, not three independent observations of the same operational interval. Retain unlocated post-list scope with null coordinates. Road and rail facilities must remain separate; no whole Moldova–Ukraine line or shared endpoint is mapped.
